# **Technical SEO Audits That Work**

## A 70-Point Checklist for Fixing What Matters Most (bonus: helpful tools)

## I. Crawlability and Indexability (High Priority)

**Why it matters:**

If search engines can’t crawl and index your site properly, none of your other SEO efforts will matter. This is the foundation of SEO success.

1\. Check robots.txt file

2\. Analyze XML sitemap

3\. Review crawl errors and blocked resources

4\. Examine index coverage

5\. Identify crawl budget issues.

6\. Ensure URLs return a 200 status code.

7\. Avoid automatic redirection.

## II. Site Architecture (High Priority)

**Why it matters:**

Good site architecture helps both users and search engines navigate your site efficiently, distributes link equity properly, and improves crawl efficiency.

8\. Evaluate internal linking

9\. Review URL structure, hierarchy and navigation

10\. Check for orphaned pages

11\. Review canonical tags

12\. Ensure no canonical/indexation mixed signal errors.

13\. Ensure important content is indexed.

## III. Page Speed and Performance (High Priority)

**Why it matters:**

Page speed is a ranking factor and directly impacts user experience, conversion rates, and bounce rates.

14\. Measure Core Web Vitals (LCP, FID, CLS)

15\. Analyze page load times

16\. Identify render-blocking resources

17\. Optimize images and resources

18\. Minimize HTTP requests

19\. Implement browser caching

## IV. Mobile-Friendliness (High Priority)

**Why it matters:**

With Google’s mobile-first indexing and the majority of searches happening on mobile devices, mobile optimization is crucial for SEO success.

20\. Test responsive design

21\. Check mobile usability issues

22\. Evaluate mobile page speed

23\. Pass Google Mobile-Friendly Test.

24\. Ensure mobile content matches desktop.

## V. HTTPS and Security (High Priority)

**Why it matters:**

A secure, HTTPS-enabled site protects user data, helps build trust, and is a known ranking signal for Google. Failure to secure your site can lead to data breaches, loss of customer confidence, and potentially lower search rankings. Proper HTTPS implementation also prevents issues such as mixed content warnings, ensuring a smooth and safe user experience.

25\. Ensure HTTPS implementation

26\. Verify SSL certificate validity

27\. Check for security vulnerabilities

## VI. Structured Data and Schema Markup (Medium Priority)

**Why it matters:**

Proper schema markup helps search engines understand your content better and can lead to enhanced search results, potentially improving click-through rates.

28\. Implement relevant schema types

29\. Test structured data implementation

30\. Review rich snippet opportunities

31\. Use OG and social metadata.

32\. Monitor rich results performance in GSC

33\. Add an “About Page” schema to better communicate with Google and optimize for the Knowledge Panel.

## VII. On-Page SEO Elements (Medium Priority)

**Why it matters:**

On-page elements are direct ranking factors and help search engines understand page context and relevance.

34\. Analyze title tags and meta descriptions

35\. Check header tag hierarchy (H1, H2, etc.)

36, Review image alt text

37\. Organize content with hierarchical HTML tags.

38\. Ensure keywords are targeted appropriately.

## VIII. Content Quality and Optimization (Medium Priority)

**Why it matters:**

High-quality, well-optimized content is essential for rankings and user engagement. It’s the foundation of organic search success.

39\. Improve EEAT (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness) signals.

40\. Identify thin or duplicate content

41\. Check for keyword cannibalization

42\. Analyze content relevance and depth

43\. Ensure content complies with Google Quality Guidelines.

44\. Avoid intrusive interstitials and heavy ads.

45\. Analyze content gap opportunities

## IX. International SEO (If Applicable) (Medium Priority)

**Why it matters:**

Proper international SEO implementation ensures your content reaches the right audience in different markets and prevents duplicate content issues.

46\. Review hreflang implementation

47\. Check for proper language targeting

48\. Analyze international site structure

## IX. International SEO (If Applicable) (Medium Priority)

**Why it matters:**

Proper international SEO implementation ensures your content reaches the right audience in different markets and prevents duplicate content issues.

46\. Review hreflang implementation

47\. Check for proper language targeting

48\. Analyze international site structure

## X. JavaScript SEO (Medium Priority)

**Why it matters:**

With modern websites heavily relying on JavaScript, ensuring proper rendering and crawling of dynamic content is crucial for SEO success.

49\. Evaluate rendering of JavaScript content

50\. Check for crawlable links and content

51\. Analyze progressive enhancement

52\. Use pagination in HTML rather than JavaScript.

## XI. Backlink Profile (Medium Priority)

**Why it matters:**

Quality backlinks remain one of the strongest ranking factors. A healthy backlink profile helps establish authority and improve rankings.

53\. Analyze backlink quality and quantity

54\. Identify toxic or spammy links

55\. Check for broken backlinks

56\. Ensure backlinks are relevant.

57\. Ensure the disavow file doesn’t block important links.

## XII. Site Migrations and Redirects (High Priority if Applicable)

**Why it matters:**

Proper migration handling prevents loss of rankings and traffic, ensuring seamless transition between old and new sites.

58\. Review redirect chains and loops

59\. Check for broken internal and external links

60\. Analyze redirect implementation

## XIII. Log File Analysis (Low Priority)

**Why it matters:**

Log file analysis provides direct insight into how search engines interact with your site, helping optimize crawl efficiency.

61\. Analyze search engine bot behavior

62\. Review crawl frequency and depth

## XIV. Images & Videos (Medium Priority)

**Why it matters:**

Properly optimized media improves page speed, user experience, and can drive additional traffic through image/video search.

63\. Optimize images for performance and SEO (e.g., compression, formats).

64\. Ensure images contain descriptive alt attributes.

65\. Define image heights and widths.

66\. Ensure video is included in the video sitemap.

67\. Implement video schema markup.

## XV. Analytics & Monitoring (High Priority)

**Why it matters:**

Proper analytics setup ensures you can track SEO performance and make data-driven decisions.

68\. Ensure analytics are installed.

69\. Verify search engine properties are set up.

70\. Run regular site crawls.

# **Helpful Tools for Technical SEO Audits**

## All-in-One SEO Suites

1\. [Semrush](https://www.semrush.com/): Offers comprehensive site auditing capabilities with over 130 technical and SEO checks.

2\. [Ahrefs](https://ahrefs.com/): Provides in-depth site audits with actionable insights and competitive analysis features

3\. [Moz](https://moz.com/): Delivers powerful link analysis and domain authority metrics alongside technical SEO tools.

## Crawling Tools

4\. [Screaming Frog SEO Spider](https://www.screamingfrog.co.uk/seo-spider/): A versatile desktop crawler that analyzes URLs, meta data, and technical SEO elements.

5\. [Sitebulb](https://sitebulb.com/): Offers visual crawl diagrams and detailed technical SEO audits with clear explanations.

6\. [Lumar](https://www.lumar.io/): Enterprise-level crawling solution with advanced JavaScript rendering capabilities.

7\. [JetOctopus](https://jetoctopus.com/) (): Cloud-based crawler specializing in large-scale websites and log file analysis.

## Search Visibility & Analytics

8\. [Google Search Console](https://search.google.com/search-console): Provides essential search performance data and technical issues directly from Google.

9\. [Google Analytics 4](https://analytics.google.com/): Tracks user behavior and provides valuable insights about website performance.

## Performance & Speed

10\. [Google PageSpeed Insights](https://pagespeed.web.dev/): Analyzes page speed and provides optimization recommendations for both mobile and desktop.

11\. [GTmetrix](https://gtmetrix.com/): Offers detailed performance reports with actionable recommendations.

12\. [Lighthouse](https://developers.google.com/web/tools/lighthouse): Provides automated auditing for performance, accessibility, and SEO.

13\. [WebPageTest](https://www.webpagetest.org/): Allows testing from multiple locations and devices with detailed performance metrics.

14\. [Pingdom](https://tools.pingdom.com/): Monitors website uptime and provides speed analysis from different geographic locations.

## Mobile & Cross-Device

15\. [Google Mobile-Friendly Test](https://search.google.com/test/mobile-friendly): Tests if your website is optimized for mobile devices.

16\. [BrowserStack](https://www.browserstack.com/): Enables testing across multiple browsers and devices.

## Security & SSL

17\. [Qualys SSL Labs](https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/): Performs deep analysis of SSL/TLS configurations.

18\. [SecurityHeaders.com](https://securityheaders.com/): Analyzes HTTP response headers and security configurations.

19\. [Sucuri SiteCheck](https://sitecheck.sucuri.net/): Scans websites for security issues and malware.

20 [Mozilla Observatory](https://observatory.mozilla.org/): Tests website security with a focus on HTTPS implementation.

## Structured Data

21\. [Google’s Structured Data Testing Tool](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data): Validates and tests structured data implementation.

22\. [Schema.org](https://schema.org/): Provides comprehensive documentation for structured data markup.

## Content & On-Page

23\. [Siteliner](https://www.siteliner.com/): Checks for duplicate content across your website.

24\. [Copyscape](https://www.copyscape.com/): Helps identify potential content plagiarism issues.

25\. [SEOwind](https://seowind.io/): Assists in content optimization and keyword research.

26\. [Grammarly](https://www.grammarly.com/): Ensures content quality through grammar and style checking.

## Hreflang & International SEO

27\. [Hreflang Testing Tool](https://ahrefs.com/hreflang-generator): Validates hreflang implementation and generates proper tags.

## Developer / Debugging

28\. [Chrome DevTools](https://developers.google.com/web/tools/chrome-devtools): Provides essential debugging tools for technical SEO issues.

## Link Analysis

29\. [Majestic](https://majestic.com/): Offers detailed backlink analysis and trust flow metrics.

## Other

30\. [TinyPNG](https://tinypng.com/): Compresses images without significant quality loss to improve page load times.
